<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel app: Fortify v1, Framework v12, Prompts v0, Socialite v5, Flux Free v2, Livewire v4, Boost v2, MCP v0, Pail v1, Pint v1, Sail v1, Pest v4, PHPUnit v12.

You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain: `fluxui-development` for Flux/UI components/forms; `livewire-development` for Livewire/reactivity/wire directives; `pest-testing` for tests; `tailwindcss-development` for Tailwind/styling; `developing-with-fortify` for authentication/Fortify.

Follow existing conventions; inspect sibling files when editing. Use descriptive names and reuse components. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested. Be concise. Ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev` if frontend changes are not reflected.

Use Boost: `list-artisan-commands` for Artisan parameters; `get-absolute-url` for project URLs; `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; `database-query` only for reads; `database-schema` before migrations/models; `browser-logs` for recent logs only. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for version-specific Laravel, ecosystem, Pest, Tailwind, and Fortify documentation before code changes. Use broad topic queries; do not add package names. Query syntax: word search, AND words, `"exact phrases"`, mixed terms, or `queries=[...]`.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion: `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations and parameter type hints. Enum keys are typically TitleCase. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex. Add array-shape definitions when appropriate.

Every change must be programmatically tested. Write/update tests and run affected tests. Run minimum tests with `php artisan test --compact` and a filename/filter. Use Pest: `php artisan make:test --pest {name}`; unit tests use `--unit`. Do NOT delete tests without approval. Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues.

Use `php artisan make:` with `--no-interaction` and correct options for new files; generic PHP classes use `php artisan make:class`. Use Eloquent relationships with return types; prefer models/relationships over raw queries, avoid `DB::`, prevent N+1 with eager loading, and use query builder only for complex operations. New models need useful factories/seeders; ask about additional needs using `list-artisan-commands`. Use API Resources/versioning unless existing conventions differ. Always create Form Requests with rules and custom messages; inspect sibling request style. Use Laravel auth/authorization. Prefer named `route()` links. Queue long operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in config files; never use `env()` directly outside config; use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Use factories and existing states in tests. Follow Faker conventions.

If Vite manifest errors occur, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Laravel 12: middleware belongs in `bootstrap/app.php` via `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`; it also registers exceptions/routes. Providers: `bootstrap/providers.php`. No `app/Http/Kernel.php` or `app\Console\Kernel.php`; use `routes/console.php`; commands in `app/Console/Commands/` auto-register. Modified columns must retain all prior attributes. Eager loading supports `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Prefer model `casts()` over `$casts`, following conventions.

Flux: use `<flux:*>` when available; free edition excludes Pro. Livewire: use Alpine.js only when client-side interaction requires it; state is server-side; validate/authorize actions.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
